security_spec.violation_condition: XiangShan executes vkeccak.vi with imm5 value 24-31, causing the Keccak round constant array KECCAK_RC to be indexed beyond its defined 24 entries (ridx from 0 to roundCnt-1 where roundCnt = imm5+1, max 32); the out-of-bounds read from the RC lookup table silently returns garbage/zero constants for rounds 24-31, corrupting the Keccak permutation output without raising an illegal instruction exception
security_spec.summary: vkeccak.vi imm5 range 0-31 allows 32 rounds but Keccak-f only defines 24 round constants; OOB RC array access for imm5 >= 24 silently produces wrong hash output

location.function_name: N/A - Zvknhk BitPat object not present

findings.finding: No Zvknhk object exists in Instructions.scala. Only Zvbb and Zimop BitPat objects are defined for vector crypto. The vkeccak.vi instruction encoding is not defined, so it will fall through to the decoder default (decodeDefault), which raises an illegal instruction exception. The vulnerability condition (imm5 values 24-31 indexing KECCAK_RC out-of-bounds) cannot occur because the Keccak permution is not implemented.

The opivi (OP-I-VI) decoder table has no entry for vkeccak.vi. The table contains entries for VADD_VI, VRSUB_VI, VAND_VI, VOR_VI, VXOR_VI, VRGATHER_VI, VSLIDEUP_VI, VSLIDEDOWN_VI, Zvbb VROR_VI, VWSLL_VI, and other standard opivi instructions, but no vkeccak.vi decoding entry. Any vkeccak.vi opcode will hit the decodeDefault illegal-instruction path in DecodeUnit.scala:50-61.

The decodeDefault function correctly produces an illegal instruction signal for unrecognized opcodes. When vkeccak.vi (which has no decoding table entry) is encountered, the decoder returns FuType.X, FuOpType.X, SelImm.INVALID_INSTR, which triggers an illegal instruction exception. This is the correct architectural behavior per RISC-V spec: unimplemented opcodes must raise illegal instruction exceptions.
findings.snippet:
def decodeDefault: List[BitPat] = // illegal instruction
  List(SrcType.X, SrcType.X, SrcType.X, FuType.X, FuOpType.X, N, N, N, N, N, N, N, UopSplitType.X, SelImm.INVALID_INSTR)

findings.finding: The ISA extension string includes scalar crypto extensions (zkn, zknd, zkne, zknh, zksed, zksh, zkt) and basic vector crypto (zvbb, zvkt) but does NOT include zvknhk, zvknhb, zvknha, or zvknh. The RTL correctly declares only what is implemented. No falsification of ISA string detected.

The SEW reserved check (VSew.isReserved) is extension-agnostic. If Zvknhk were implemented in the future, this check would NOT independently enforce the Zvknha SEW restriction (e64 reserved for SHA-256) vs Zvknhb (e64 legal). However, since Zvknhk is not currently implemented, this is a forward-looking concern, not an active bug. The current check only validates SEW against the generic VSew encoder, which is correct for the instructions actually implemented.

The vstartIllegal check applies a blanket vstart != 0 restriction for all vArith instructions. If Zvknhk were implemented, vkeccak.vi would incorrectly raise illegal instruction for non-zero vstart, when the spec requires only that vstart be aligned to EGS=32 (i.e., vstart % 32 == 0). However, since Zvknhk is not implemented, this EGS-unaware check has no operational impact and only becomes relevant if Zvknhk is added in the future.
